Users report wrong sums, maxima, and threshold-search results after mixing range
updates in production. The root cause is unknown. The visible test reproduces
one sequence, but other workloads also disagree with the stored values.

Investigate and repair `src/range-tree.js`. Preserve the CommonJS named export
`RangeTree` and the complete API documented in its source comment, including
half-open ranges, error handling, and empty-range behavior. Keep O(log n) updates
and queries, O(n) construction and `toArray()`, and O(n) storage; a rewrite that
scans the affected range is not acceptable. Do not add dependencies.

Work only in the current directory. Do not modify `test/` or `package.json`.
Verify the fix with `node --test`.

content.text:
I fixed `src/range-tree.js`. There were three separate bugs: one caused the wrong sums, one the wrong maxima, and one the wrong threshold-search results. `node --test` passes 1/1.

**Fixes:**
1. **Wrong sums after assign-then-add:** `_applyAssignment` left the node's pending add in place. When that tag was later pushed down, the old add was applied again on top of the new value. This is the visible test case: assign 4 → add 3 → assign 10 → add 2 gave 10+3+2 instead of 12 per element. The fix clears `_additions[node]` when an assignment is applied, so stored tags always mean "assign first, then add", as the source comment says.
2. **Wrong maxima for negative ranges:** `_max` started its result at `0`, so a range that crossed nodes and held only negative values returned 0. It now starts at `-Infinity`.
3. **Wrong `firstAtLeast` results:** `_first` went down into child nodes without first passing pending updates to them. After a lazy update it searched stale child maxima. It now calls `_push` before going into the children.

The API, error handling, empty-range behaviour, `Float64Array` storage of 4n entries, and complexity are all unchanged; each fix is O(1). `firstAtLeast` stays O(log n): it only follows the path containing `lo` and then makes at most one successful descent, skipping everything else using the stored maxima.

**Additional check:** I also ran a throwaway randomized comparison against a plain array: 2,000 trees of size 1–20, each with 60 random `assign`/`add`/`sum`/`max`/`firstAtLeast`/`get` operations using negative and positive values, followed by a `toArray()` comparison. Everything matched; I deleted the script afterwards. I didn't run it against the old code, so I haven't confirmed it would have caught each bug on its own.
